comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA — confirmed root cause, and a correction to the reported blast radius

### Proven mechanism
scripts/gen_env_registry.py::scan recognises exactly three direct stdlib shapes -- the
os.environ[...] subscript, os.environ.get(...) (the func.attr == "get" test, now at :98
after the b00f edit shifted it), and os.getenv(...) -- plus the KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS table.
Every other expression falls through the `for node in ast.walk(tree)` loop with no branch
and no diagnostic. The fallthrough is the defect: an unrecognised os.environ access is a
silent skip, so the key it reads is simply absent from the generated registry and the
drift gate stays green because the doc still agrees with the (blind) generator.

### Discriminating experiment (dynamic -- run, not read)
Swapped opcert_service/config.py:102 from os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY") to
os.environ.pop("REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY", None) -- the one-token edit the ticket
describes -- then ran the generator:

  before: _162 variables._   REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY present
  after:  _161 variables._   REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY absent (grep count 0)
  generator exit code: 0 in both runs

That reproduces the reported 1-key drop exactly, and confirms the silence: nothing on
stdout, stderr, or the exit code distinguishes the two runs. Source restored; git diff
clean. This rules out the alternative that the key survives via another read site.

### Correction: ZERO keys are being dropped today, not one
The ticket's headline instance is already mitigated, and the audit found no second one.
A full AST census of every os.environ attribute access under src/rebar returns exactly
three attributes in use:

  os.environ.get      115 sites  (recognised)
  os.environ.pop        2 sites  (NOT recognised)
  os.environ.copy       1 site   (bulk, no literal key -- nothing to register)

Both pop sites read a key that is ALSO reached by a recognised shape in the same module,
so neither is currently lost:

  - opcert_service/config.py:106 pops REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY, but :102 still reads it
    with os.environ.get -- the deliberate workaround illusory-patronal-giraffe left in
    place, with a comment saying so.
  - _io/import_ndjson.py:393 pops REBAR_SYNC_PUSH, but :216 reads it with
    os.environ.get and :217/:395 assign it by subscript.

Also checked and found absent: any `x = os.environ` alias binding (none), and any
setdefault/getitem-with-default form (none). The five os.environ pass-by-reference sites
(dict(os.environ), project_child_env(os.environ, ...), raise_or_warn_env(os.environ)) are
bulk handoffs with no literal key, so there is nothing for the registry to record.

So AC4 is already satisfied and the count has since GROWN to 162, not 161. The defect is
LATENT, not active: the blind spot is real and reproducible on demand, but it is currently
costing zero documented keys. Fixing it is prophylactic -- which is the right call, since
the next pop-based read hits it without the giraffe ticket's luck.

### Why this is a defect and not the documented scope limit
The generator's docstring does disclaim exhaustive indirection coverage. Two authorities
override that for this case:
1. Its own stated invariant, same docstring: "a CI drift gate regenerates it and fails the
   build on any diff, so a new env-var read cannot ship undocumented." A pop-based read
   ships undocumented AND green. The invariant is violated, not merely unfulfilled.
2. Prior closed Fixed: bug b00f-c62e-d3b9-4e63 (scared-restored-swallow, closed
   2026-08-01) is the same class -- a read shape invisible to the scanner producing
   undocumented vars -- and was accepted as a defect then. Its own commit message records
   the class as still open: "A missing row is not an error, it is invisible ... a clean
   --check proves the doc AGREES with the generator, never that it is COMPLETE."

Classification: defect (specifically an omission -- a guard that was never written).

### Defect origin -- caused_by 0f21-ca03-f063-4562
git blame -w -C -M -L 95,102 puts the recogniser on c1f17861ec2d9ea2b55b82990dba22cda446d74b
(2026-07-08, "feat(maint): generated REBAR_* env-var registry with a CI drift gate",
rebar-ticket: 0f21-ca03-f063-4562). Confirmed against the commit's own blob: the narrow
recogniser and the silent fallthrough are present in the file's FIRST version, so there is
no carrier commit to walk through and no good->bad transition to bisect.

Date test applied: the implicated lines do not predate a transition, because there was no
transition -- the behaviour was never right. This is the omission case, so the attribution
is by introducing commit AND by scope of work: 0f21's plan enumerated the read-pattern set
and chose a silent skip for everything else, and 0f21's own acceptance language ("a new
env-var read cannot ship undocumented") is the invariant this gap breaks. A reviewer on
0f21 could plausibly have caught it.

Considered and rejected as the origin: b00f-c62e-d3b9-4e63. It touched the same file most
recently (ecb9149412, 2026-08-01) and a naive whole-file blame majority leans that way,
but it only ADDED a KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS row -- it did not create the fallthrough and did not
make any previously-correct behaviour wrong. Recording the divergence from the blame
default per protocol. Close class will be plan_defect, not regression.

### Caller-dependency sweep
scripts/check_config_ownership.py:164 does `reads, _dynamic = scan(...)` -- the only
non-test consumer of scan(). The fix must preserve the 2-tuple arity (it will; the
fail-closed signal is an exception, not a third element). Post-fix scan() output over the
CURRENT tree is byte-identical, because both pop keys are already registered via their
sibling .get reads -- so the config-ownership gate sees no change today. Incidental
dependency only; no behavioural dependency on the current narrowness. Gate cleared.

comments.body:
## Phase 2 report — fixed, Gerrit 1979

### Fix
scripts/gen_env_registry.py now classifies EVERY os.environ attribute access, called or
not, instead of matching one accessor and walking past the rest.

RECOGNISED as key-bearing (register the string-literal first argument):
  get, pop, setdefault, __getitem__   -- plus the existing os.environ["X"] subscript and
  os.getenv("X"), and the KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS table, all unchanged.
  pop and setdefault both RETURN the current value, so both are reads.
  __getitem__ earns its place from review, not from the report: an explicit
  os.environ.__getitem__("X") is an ast.Call, not an ast.Subscript, so the subscript branch
  never sees it. Classifying it as bulk would have left a hole of exactly the kind this
  ticket exists to close.

ALLOWED as bulk, registering nothing (they name no single variable):
  copy, items, keys, values, update, clear, popitem, __contains__, __iter__, __len__,
  __setitem__, __delitem__. Each carries a comment saying why. __setitem__/__delitem__ are
  key-bearing but WRITE-only; the os.environ["X"] = v Store subscript stays registered as
  it was, deliberately preserved rather than "corrected" inside a bug fix.

ANYTHING ELSE raises UnrecognisedEnvironAccess listing every offending path:line in one
message. This is the half that matters: enumerating accessors can only cover forms someone
thought of, and the ticket asked for the form nobody predicted to fail the build.

DELIBERATELY NOT recognised, and documented as such in both the module docstring and the
generated header rather than pretended-covered:
  - reads under tests/ (outside the scan root by design)
  - non-literal keys -- REPORTED in the dynamic list rather than dropped, now for pop and
    setdefault as well as get
  - os.environ passed by reference (dict(os.environ), f(os.environ)) -- a bulk handoff
    with no literal key, indistinguishable from an allowed whole-mapping access
  - getattr(os.environ, "get")(...) string indirection -- not statically resolvable at all

scan() keeps its 2-tuple arity on purpose: scripts/check_config_ownership.py:164 unpacks
it. The fail-closed signal is the exception, never a third return element.

### RED -> GREEN, held out
Oracle: tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py (+90 lines, append-only -- the diff has ZERO
deleted lines, so no pre-existing assertion was weakened).

RED first, 4 failing for the right reasons before any fix existed: pop and setdefault
absent from reads; UnrecognisedEnvironAccess not existing at all; a non-literal pop absent
from dynamic. The bulk-access and count-pin cases were green from the start -- they are
invariant guards, and were written to stay green.

The oracle was moved OUT of the tree before the implementing subagent was launched, which
was given only the mechanism and a frozen contract card. Re-applied afterwards: 16/16
green against a test it never saw. A 17th (the __getitem__ case) came from my own review
of the returned diff and went through the same RED -> GREEN.

MUTATION (teeth), each restored afterwards:
  - re-narrow KEY_BEARING to {"get"}, i.e. re-seed the exact original defect
        -> 6 RED. Note the interlock: re-narrowing now ALSO trips the fail-closed guard on
           the real tree, because the two live os.environ.pop sites become unclassifiable.
           The defect can no longer be reintroduced quietly.
  - delete the raise, restoring the silent skip
        -> 1 RED (DID NOT RAISE), precisely the fail-closed test.
  - move __getitem__ back out of the key-bearing set
        -> RED.
No mutation left the suite green.

### Replication of the original report
The report's own one-token edit, re-run against the fixed generator:
  os.environ.get -> os.environ.pop at opcert_service/config.py:102
  BEFORE the fix: 162 -> 161 keys, REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY gone, exit 0.
  AFTER  the fix: 162 keys, key present.
And a form nobody enumerated (os.environ.take_it("...")) now aborts:
  UnrecognisedEnvironAccess: - os.environ.take_it at src/rebar/opcert_service/config.py:102
  generator exit code: 1
Source restored; git diff clean.

### Artifact
docs/env-vars.md WAS regenerated and is in the same change. The table and the 162-key count
are byte-identical -- only the header prose changed, because it is generated from the
recogniser sets and now states the fail-closed contract and its boundary. CI asserts the
artifact matches the generator in the `Env-var registry drift gate` step of
.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml and in
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys.

### Local/CI agreement (AC3)
`python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check` added to the `lint:` target (~0.55 s), grouped
with the other portable script gates. It does double-run against the docs-gates step; that
is the deliberate trade, and it is the same shape as the config gates already in that
target. Local `make lint` now reports staleness that previously appeared only in the full
suite or in CI.

One collateral repair: tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py builds a sandbox repo
and runs the committed Makefile in it, stubbing each gate that precedes the guard under
test. A new `make lint` gate needs a stub there or the run aborts early on a missing
script. Added the stub and extended the comment to say so, so the next person adding a gate
is not surprised. Found by the full sweep, not by make lint.

### Scope and safety
- Caller sweep: check_config_ownership.py is the only non-test consumer of scan(); arity
  preserved and its scan() output over the current tree is unchanged, since both pop keys
  are already registered via their sibling .get reads. Incidental, not behavioural.
- Restoration, not creation: no new entry point, artifact, or external call.
- No new dependency (ast/argparse/sys/pathlib were already imported).
- No test weakened: the only pre-existing test touched gained a stub line and a comment.

### Gates
make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (613 files); complexity ratchet
active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0. scan() went 17 -> 5 by extraction into _record /
_scan_call / _scan_module (7/7/3), so the file now has no C901 violation at all -- it did
before this change. Full unit sweep: 11950 passed, 44 skipped, 0 failed, 0 errors.
(An earlier sweep showed 3 failures and 16 errors; the 16 were _no_repo_commits teardown
errors caused by my own commit landing mid-run, and 2 of the 3 were the same race. Re-run
with HEAD stable to be sure rather than assumed. The 3rd was the real criteria-vocabulary
regression fixed above.)

### Siblings (Step 7)
CONSTRUCT axis, bounded: the class is "an AST recogniser that enumerates accepted shapes
and silently skips the rest". The other AST scanners under scripts/ (check_comment_hygiene,
check_raw_git_writes, check_wall_clock_asserts, check_config_reads, mutation_gate,
check_complexity_baseline) are violation DETECTORS -- failing open there means a missed
finding, not a published artifact that claims completeness. None builds a registry from an
enumerated read-shape set. I did not audit their individual recognisers; that is the
boundary of this sweep.

PARITY axis: rule = "every key-bearing os.environ access must document its variable".
CLI / MCP / library facade: N/A, this is a build script with no such surface.
Automated callers: check_config_ownership.py -- routes through the shared scan(), so it
INHERITS the fix and the fail-closed behaviour; not a MISSING slot.
Dual direction: the mirror operation is env WRITE detection, which the registry does not
claim to cover. No MISSING slots.

### Residual risk
1. The blind spot's SECOND half is untouched and I want it recorded rather than implied
   fixed: KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS is still fail-OPEN. A project helper absent from that table is
   invisible exactly as before -- that is bug b00f's own finding, still true, and the
   comment in the file still says so. Fail-closed now covers os.environ, not helper
   indirection. Filing this as follow-up work rather than widening this change.
2. Accepted: the make lint / docs-gates double-run (~0.55 s), for the AC3 local signal.

comments.body:
Landed as Gerrit 1979 (PS2), merged to main as 9b1d2e6808 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Verified on the merged tree: the widened key-bearing set and the make lint drift check are present, and the 17 oracle cases pass.

Two code-review findings on PS1, both addressed:
- BLOCKING bugfix-size-attestation: 247 non-test lines, over the 150-line floor, with no plan-review attestation on this ticket. My error -- I went into Phase 2 without running review-plan. Corrected file_impact to name all five paths I actually touch (the two test files were missing) and ran the review: PASS, signed, 0 blocking, 2 deferred advisories.
- Advisory, and a real defect in the diff: the _scan_call docstring pointed at a function _scan_environ_attribute that does not exist. Classification actually happens inline in _scan_module. Rewritten to say where it happens and why (_scan_module sees the ast.Attribute node whether or not it is called).

Worth recording: one deferred advisory (G1G2) asked whether fail-closing would newly implicate the pre-existing os.environ writes at _io/import_ndjson.py:217/:393/:395. It does not, and the implementation already answers it -- the subscript Store form is registered by the Subscript branch and pop is key-bearing, so REBAR_SYNC_PUSH resolves through both. Confirmed by the generator running clean on the merged tree.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py` recognises only a closed set of environment-read forms when it scans
`src/rebar` to build `docs/env-vars.md`. At `scripts/gen_env_registry.py:98` it matches
`func.attr == "get"` (plus the `os.environ[...]` subscript and `os.getenv` forms). Any OTHER
expression that reads an environment variable is invisible to it.

The consequence is silent documentation loss on a refactor that looks entirely harmless. Changing

```python
value = os.environ.get("REBAR_SOMETHING")
```

to

```python
value = os.environ.pop("REBAR_SOMETHING", None)
```

still reads the variable, but the generator no longer sees it, so the key DISAPPEARS from
`docs/env-vars.md`. Nothing about the edit signals that documentation was dropped.

## Evidence
Observed 2026-08-20 while implementing `illusory-patronal-giraffe` (op-cert credential hardening).
The natural implementation of that ticket was exactly the `get` -> `pop` swap. It silently reduced
the generated registry from **161 keys to 160**, dropping `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` — the very
variable the change was about.

The implementer worked around it rather than absorbing a generator fix: the read stays an
`os.environ.get` with a literal key, and the pop is a SEPARATE statement. That is the correct scope
call for that ticket and it is not in question here — but it leaves the generator blind spot in
place, and the next person to write a `pop`-based read will hit it without the same luck.

## Why the current gate does not protect you
`make lint` does NOT catch this. The staleness check only fires in the full suite, via
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys`.

So the feedback loop is: make a reasonable one-token edit, see `make lint` pass locally, and learn
about the dropped documentation from CI — or not at all, if the same change happens to regenerate
the file. This is the same shape as the complexity-ratchet divergence recorded on
`dystopian-bardlike-basil`: a local gate that is weaker than CI, teaching contributors to trust a
signal that does not hold.

## Investigation before choosing a remedy
Establish first which env-read forms actually occur, or plausibly could, in `src/rebar` — `pop`,
`setdefault`, an `os.environ` alias bound to a local name, a `dict(os.environ)` copy, indirect reads
through a helper. The remedy should be sized to what the codebase realistically uses, not to every
expression Python permits.

Candidate approaches, to be decided on evidence:
- Widen the recogniser to the read-bearing method set (`get`, `pop`, `setdefault`, …) rather than
  the single `get`.
- Make an UNRECOGNISED `os.environ` attribute access a loud generator error rather than a silent
  skip, so a novel form fails the build instead of quietly dropping a key. This is the fail-closed
  option and is likely stronger than enumerating methods, since it catches forms nobody predicted.
- Have `make lint` run the generator's `--check` so the local and CI verdicts agree.

The second and third are complementary: fail-closed recognition plus a local gate that actually
reports it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A `pop`-based environment read in `src/rebar` is REGISTERED in `docs/env-vars.md` — proven by
      a test that performs the read one way, regenerates, and asserts the key is present; and that
      FAILS against today's generator.
- [x] An `os.environ` access the recogniser does not understand causes a LOUD failure (generator
      error or a failing check), not a silent omission. Proven with a deliberately novel form.
- [x] The local and CI verdicts agree: a tree whose generated registry is stale fails
      `make lint`, not only the full suite. If that is judged too slow for the lint path, record
      why and name where the earlier signal comes from instead.
- [x] `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` remains present in `docs/env-vars.md` (key count does not regress
      from 161), guarding the specific instance that exposed this.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` pass, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

## Provenance
Discovered 2026-08-20 during `illusory-patronal-giraffe`; the generator behaviour at
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py:98` and the 161→160 key drop were both observed directly, not inferred.

file_impact.reason: The recogniser: widen to the key-bearing accessors (get/pop/setdefault/__getitem__) and fail closed on any other os.environ attribute instead of silently skipping it.
The generated artifact; regenerated so its header states the widened, fail-closed contract. Table and 162-key count unchanged.
Run the generator --check in the lint target so the local verdict matches CI.
RED->GREEN oracle for every recognised shape, the loud failure on an unknown one, and the bulk/dynamic invariants.
Its sandbox runs the committed Makefile and stubs each gate preceding the guard under test; a new make lint gate needs a stub there or the run aborts early.

compiled_state.title: gen_env_registry recognises only os.environ.get, so a pop-based read silently drops its key from docs/env-vars.md
